doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The candy store on 3rd Street
summary: McLean bought a candy store with his sons' savings and advertised it from the Slug's stage.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you get the store on 3rd Street?

Maybe a year or so later. It happened because I wanted to take my sons, their money, and invest it in something and put some money to what they had saved and so something with it. What I did was buy this candy store and sell cigarettes and candy and malteds and ice cream and just generally – a candy store. Then I would sell it at Slug’s, when I’d leave the stage. Say, “Ladies and gentlemen, when you’re going on your break, just go right down the street, get yourself a refreshing malted ice cream sundae, buy a few candy bars, and be back for the next set.” That’s how I used to do that.
